answers.plain:
**Subject:** Plus plan pricing update, effective January 1

Hi {{first_name}},

We're writing to let you know that the price of the Plus plan will change from $12 to $15 per month, starting January 1. This email gives you 30 days' notice, so you have time to plan.

Here's what's behind the change. Over the past year we've made Plus more valuable:

- **Weekly backups:** your data is now backed up automatically every week.
- **Double the storage:** you now have twice the space you had before.

The new price reflects those improvements and lets us keep investing in the features and reliability you count on.

**If you're on an annual plan,** nothing changes for now. You'll keep your current rate until your plan renews.

If you'd like to review or change your plan, you can do that anytime in your account settings: {{account_link}}. Questions? Just reply to this email and we'll be happy to help.

Thank you for being a Plus subscriber. We appreciate you.

Best,
{{sender_name}}
{{company_name}}

---

Notes:
- Today is Oct 26, so a notice sent by Dec 2 would still give a full 30 days before Jan 1. Send it soon if you want a comfortable margin.
- I left placeholders for the name, account link, and sign-off. I also didn't state when the backups and storage were added, since I don't know the dates. Add them if you'd like.
answers.nudge:
# Email draft

**Subject options** (pick one)
1. Plus is changing to $15/month on January 1
2. An update to Plus pricing, effective January 1
3. What's new in Plus, and a pricing update

I'd go with #1. It's plain and specific, and it won't read like a bait-and-switch.

**Preview text:** Weekly backups and double the storage are already live. Here's what changes on January 1.

---

Hi [First name],

Starting **January 1**, the Plus plan will go from **$12 to $15 per month**. You're getting this email now so you have at least 30 days to plan for it.

**Why the change**
Plus has grown a lot since you joined. Over the past [few months], we've added:

- **Weekly backups**, so your work is automatically protected and recoverable.
- **Double the storage**, from [X GB] to [2X GB], at no extra charge so far.

Those upgrades are already live on your account. The new price lets us keep investing in them and in the reliability behind them.

**What this means for you**
- **Monthly subscribers:** Your first charge at the new rate will be on [your first billing date on or after January 1]. You don't need to do anything to continue.
- **Annual subscribers:** Your current rate stays the same until your plan renews.
- If Plus no longer fits your needs, you can change or cancel anytime in [Account Settings → Billing]. There are no fees and no hoops.

If you have questions, just reply to this email. A real person will answer.

Thanks for being a Plus member.

[Name]
[Title], [Company]

---

# Notes before you send

- **Send deadline:** To give a full 30 days before January 1, this must go out **by December 2**. Earlier is safer. Today is Oct 26, so you have room to send it in November.
- **Placeholders to fill in:** storage amounts, the time frame for when the upgrades shipped, the billing-settings path, and the sender.
- **Billing-date wording needs a check.** I assumed monthly subscribers pay $15 from their first renewal on or after January 1. If your billing system works differently, for example if it prorates, fix that line. Billing ambiguity is the most common source of angry replies after a price change.
- **Tone choices:**
  - It states the change in the first sentence, with no "unfortunately" and no "we regret."
  - The price is tied to the value already delivered.
  - Nothing apologizes. The only acknowledgment is "so you have time to plan," which is respectful rather than apologetic.
- **Annual-plan line:** I wrote it as reassurance, since this email goes to monthly subscribers. If you'd like to give monthly subscribers an option to switch to annual, add a line with the annual price. Only do that if the offer exists. I didn't invent one.
- **Follow-up:** Consider a short reminder around December 20 to monthly subscribers. It costs little and reduces surprise-charge support tickets.
- **Support prep:** Give your support team a short FAQ before sending. The likely questions are about prorating, refunds for charges on or after January 1, and annual renewal pricing.
